purpose: REST API (.NET 10, Minimal APIs): register, login, JWT + single-use refresh tokens with reuse detection, roles User/Admin, admin-only paginated user list, rate limiting on /auth.

stack.auth: JwtBearer (HS256) + ASP.NET Core Identity (AddIdentityCore, Guid keys)
stack.tests: xUnit integration tests against a real DB container (both engines, selected with TEST_DB_PROVIDER); WebApplicationFactory<Program>

layers.name: ApiUsers.Domain
contains: RefreshToken (IsActive, Revoke; FamilyId groups a rotation chain)

layers.name: ApiUsers.Application
contains: DTOs in Auth/AuthDtos.cs (RegisterRequest, LoginRequest, RefreshRequest, TokenResponse, UserResponse), PagedResponse<T>, RegistrationResult/RegistrationStatus
rules: Must not reference UserManager or EF Core

layers.name: ApiUsers.Infrastructure
contains: IdentityService : IIdentityService (wraps UserManager, lockout, roles, paging, decoy hash on failed paths, duplicate-registration race handling)
JwtTokenGenerator : ITokenGenerator (HS256 JWT, 32 random bytes refresh value, SHA-256 hash)
RefreshTokenRepository : IRefreshTokenRepository (atomic TryRotate via ExecuteUpdate, RevokeFamily)
AppDbContext, AppUser, AppRole, DatabaseOptions, DatabaseExtensions (provider switch, MigrateDatabaseAsync, SeedDatabaseAsync), DbSeeder
DependencyInjection.AddInfrastructure (Identity options incl. password length 10 and lockout, JwtOptions validation, DI registrations)
rules: Must not reference Api or the Migrations projects

layers.name: ApiUsers.Migrations.SqlServer / ApiUsers.Migrations.PostgreSql
contains: One EF migration set per engine (InitialCreate each)
rules: Selected by assembly name in DatabaseExtensions.AddAppDatabase; a model change needs a migration in BOTH projects

layers.name: ApiUsers.Api
contains: Program.cs (composition root, middleware order, public partial class Program)
Auth/AuthEndpoints.cs, Users/UserEndpoints.cs (input validation + HTTP mapping only)
Auth/JwtAuthenticationExtensions.cs (JwtBearer params: MapInboundClaims=false, ClockSkew=0, only HS256, NameClaim=sub, RoleClaim=role)
Security/RateLimitingExtensions.cs (sliding window per client IP on /auth/*, 429 + Retry-After)
Security/ForwardedHeadersExtensions.cs (opt-in trust of X-Forwarded-For/Proto for listed proxies only)

dependencyDirection: Api -> Application -> Domain; Api -> Infrastructure -> Application; Migrations.* -> Infrastructure. Enforced by tests/ArchitectureTests.cs.
startupPipeline: Services: AddApplication, AddInfrastructure, AddJwtAuthentication, AddAppRateLimiting, AddAppForwardedHeaders, AddOpenApi
MigrateDatabaseAsync then SeedDatabaseAsync (both only if Database:MigrateOnStartup = true)
UseRateLimiter, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, then map endpoints

endpoints.notes: Always role User. Email max 256, password 10..128. Simultaneous registrations of the same email give one 201 and the rest 409.
Single generic 401 for unknown email / bad password / locked account.
Revokes family only if token belongs to caller; idempotent.
Always re-read from store (token may outlive account).

endpoints.auth: bearer + role Admin (re-checked in the store)

keyFlows.login: Endpoint validates -> AuthService.LoginAsync -> IIdentityService.ValidateCredentialsAsync -> new RefreshToken (new FamilyId) stored as hash -> JWT access token (15 min) + plain refresh value (7 days) returned.
keyFlows.refresh: Hash incoming token -> FindByHash. Missing: null. Revoked: RevokeFamily (theft) + null. Expired: null. Account locked/deleted (GetUserIfCanSignIn): null. TryRotate (atomic): on lost race RevokeFamily + null. Success: new token in same family.
keyFlows.logout: Find by hash; if owned by caller, RevokeFamily. Always 204 if authenticated.
keyFlows.seeding: DbSeeder creates roles User/Admin and admin from Admin:Email/Admin:Password. Existing non-admin account with that email is promoted only if password matches; otherwise warning logged and startup continues.

configuration.Database:MigrateOnStartup: bool, default false (true in Development); gates migrations AND seeding
configuration.Jwt:Issuer / Audience / SigningKey / Acc: validated on start; SigningKey >= 32 bytes, secret
configuration.RateLimiting:AuthPermitLimit / AuthWindo: requests per client IP per sliding window on /auth/*; defaults 20 / 60
configuration.ForwardedHeaders:Enabled / KnownProxies: default off; when on, at least one known proxy or network is required or startup fails
configuration.docker: docker-compose.yml: sqlserver (default), postgres (profile 'postgres'); secrets from .env (not versioned)

securityDecisions: Refresh tokens stored only as SHA-256 hash; single use; reuse revokes the whole family
Rotation is atomic (conditional ExecuteUpdate) so concurrent use yields exactly one success
Lockout after 5 failures for 5 minutes; generic 401 to avoid user enumeration; unknown email and locked account both pay a decoy password hash
Password: minimum 10 characters plus Identity's default complexity rules
Refresh refuses locked-out accounts; GET /users re-checks the Admin role in the store instead of trusting only the token claim
Rate limit on /auth/*: sliding window per client IP, in memory (per instance)
Forwarded headers are opt-in and only from listed proxies, so clients cannot fake their IP
HSTS and HTTPS redirection outside Development
Admin never hardcoded; comes from configuration
knownLimitations: No email confirmation (anyone can register someone else's email)
409 on register reveals that an email exists
Expired/revoked refresh tokens are never purged
Single HS256 signing key, no kid / key rotation window
Rate limit counters are per instance (no shared store)

helpers: ApiFactory (container per engine, rate limit and token lifetimes pinned)
StartupAssert (startup must fail with OptionsValidationException naming the key)
tests.count: 129 tests (integration, unit, architecture); run with `dotnet test` and `TEST_DB_PROVIDER=PostgreSql dotnet test`

howToAddAFeature: 1. Domain: add entity/rule only if it has behavior independent of storage.
2. Application: add use case in a service + port interface for any storage/crypto/IO need + DTOs.
3. Infrastructure: implement the port, register it in DependencyInjection.AddInfrastructure; extend AppDbContext if needed.
4. If the schema changed: add a migration in BOTH Migrations.SqlServer and Migrations.PostgreSql.
5. Api: add endpoint under a Map* extension, validate input there, map results to HTTP, declare Produces*/ProducesProblem, call it from Program.cs.
6. Tests: add integration tests, keep ArchitectureTests green, run against both providers.
pitfalls: Do not use UserManager or EF types in Application.
Endpoints use nullable request records on purpose so malformed bodies return 400 instead of failing binding.
JwtBearer MapInboundClaims=false: read claims as 'sub' and 'role', not ClaimTypes.*.
MigrateOnStartup=false by default: seeding does not run unless it is enabled.
Do not enable ForwardedHeaders without listing the proxies: an empty list would make the framework trust every client.
Tests need a high RateLimiting:AuthPermitLimit (ApiFactory sets it) because the suite makes many /auth calls from one address.
